title: Make your profile look like you

items.title: Background colours stay the colour you pick
items.text: Edit profile → Look → Background → Colour now paints your page in exactly the colour you chose, light or dark, pastel or neon. The text turns light or dark by itself so it stays readable. There are more colours to pick from too, including black, white and pastels.

items.title: Profile style
items.text: Under Look → Style, pick Panels (Lilin's own look), Soft (rounded cards) or Minimal (no boxes, just your background).

items.title: Background patterns
items.text: Under Look → Pattern, lay a faint texture over your background: dots, grid, stripes, grain, stars or hearts.

items.title: Tidier See all links
items.text: See all likes, More reviews, More activity and the rest are now small links under each section on a profile instead of big full-width rows.

items.title: Picture ring follows your accent
items.text: The ring around your picture on your profile now takes the accent you picked in Edit profile instead of the app theme's colour.

title: Your anime list on your profile

items.title: Link MyAnimeList or AniList
items.text: In Edit profile, add your MyAnimeList or AniList username (or both). Your profile gets an Anime section with what you're watching there, what you finished lately and your numbers, plus a link in the header. It updates by itself every few hours. The list has to be public.

items.title: Usernames instead of emails
items.text: You can now sign in with your @username and password. New people pick a username when they join and never have to give an email.

items.title: Drop your email
items.text: Joined with an email? It still works for now. When you're ready, go to You, then Account, then Switch to a username: you sign in with your username from then on and Lilin deletes your email. Your history, friends and settings stay.

title: A diary of what you really watched

items.title: Peeking doesn't count
items.text: Opening an episode or film for a few seconds to look around no longer puts it in your diary or profile. It shows up once you've actually watched a real part of it.

items.title: Drag the whole preview
items.text: In Edit profile, grab anywhere on the preview card at the top (picture, name or face) and drag up or down to choose which part of your banner shows.

items.title: No more jumping title
items.text: Resting the pointer on a poster opens its card with the title's logo already in place, instead of showing the name first and swapping in the logo a moment later.

items.title: Your own banner picture
items.text: Edit profile → Look → Banner → Upload puts any photo of yours at the top of your profile. Drag it in the preview (or use the slider) to choose which part shows. Only people who can see your profile see it.

items.title: Profile colours
items.text: Look → Background → Colour paints your whole profile page in a colour you pick. Turn Gradient on to blend two colours down the page, or off for one solid colour. Lilin adjusts the shade so the text stays easy to read, in light and dark themes.

items.title: A status, a pinned review and your numbers
items.text: Add a short status under your name (it can clear itself after a day or a week), pin one of your reviews to the top of your profile, and pick which numbers show under your name (films, shows, hours, reviews, likes and more).

items.title: Read more on long reviews
items.text: A review too long to fit on a title page or a profile now ends with Read more. Tap it to read the whole thing right there, and Show less to fold it back.

items.title: Read reviews on the TV app
items.text: A film or show's page in the TV app now has a Reviews row with everything people wrote about it on Lilin, plus the average stars. Press OK on a review to read all of it; left and right go to the next one. Spoilers stay hidden until you open them. Writing a review still happens on the website.

title: Search finds the one you mean

items.title: Well-known titles come first in search
items.text: Search now weighs how well known a film or show is, not just whether the name matches exactly. Type endgame and you get Avengers: Endgame first instead of a row of forgotten films that happen to be called Endgame. Add a year (like Endgame 2015) when you want a specific one.

title: Keep a title off your profile

items.title: Hide a film or show from your profile
items.text: On a film or show's page, open the ⋯ menu and pick Hide from my profile. Other people then won't see it on your profile: not in Recent activity, your diary, Liked, Reviews or Taste match, and your face isn't shown among the people who liked it. You still see everything, and it still counts in your own history: on your own profile hidden titles are faded with an eye mark, and a Hidden from others shelf at the bottom lists them all. Pick Show on my profile to bring one back.

items.title: No squashed pages
items.text: Opening a page for the first time, like Activity or Game clips under House, no longer shows it squashed for a moment. Pages now simply fade in.

title: Stay for the scene after the credits

items.title: Know when there's a scene after the credits
items.text: Films with a scene during or after the credits now say so: a small line on the film's page and when you pause, and when the credits start the end card says "Stay: there's a scene after the credits" before the picture comes back full size. In Watch Together everyone in the room sees it too, so nobody leaves too early. Films without the note may still have one: Lilin only says it when it knows.

title: New episodes that just came out

items.title: New episodes this week shows what actually aired
items.text: The New episodes this week row on Discover now shows series that just put out an episode, like a show releasing weekly, with the newest and most watched first. No more talk shows and soaps. Each card says which episode came out and when, and a New episode tag stays on for a week. A season or series that just started is tagged New season or New series for a month.

items.title: Your New episodes row goes by release date
items.text: The New episodes row with your own shows now only lists a show when a new episode actually came out in the last two weeks and you haven't seen it, not when an old episode happened to land on Lilin. The tag just says New episodes.

items.title: New tag on episodes
items.text: On a show's page, episodes that came out in the last week have a New tag, until you've watched them.

items.title: No more flicker when you switch tabs
items.text: Going back to Discover no longer flashes the film's name in plain text for a split second before its logo appears, and opening Live for the first time no longer shows the page squashed before it settles.

title: LikLok: scroll clips, find your next show

items.title: A feed of the best bits from shows on Lilin
items.text: The new LikLok tab is a feed of short clips from the first episodes of the shows on Lilin. Swipe up for the next one; tap once for sound. Like what you see? Keep watching opens the episode right where the clip is, so the scene just carries on, or start from episode 1. You can also put the show on My list, open its page, or say Not for me and it stops showing up. The feed learns from what you watch to the end and what you swipe past, and puts shows you haven't started first. Clips only come from the start of a show, so nothing gets spoiled.

title: Find a film by a line from it

items.title: Search for a line someone says
items.text: Type a line you half remember in Search, like "I drink your milkshake" or "pivot", and a new Lines group shows the films and episodes on Lilin where it's said, with the picture from that moment and the lines around it. Tap one and it plays from a few seconds before the line. Handy for settling which episode a joke was in, or for showing someone that one scene.

items.title: See how close your taste is to a friend's
items.text: Open a friend's profile to see your Taste match, from Low to Super, worked out from the stars and thumbs you've both given the same films and shows (it needs 10 in common). Under it: what you both loved, where you split, and what they loved that you haven't seen yet. A thumbs down on its own still stays private. Only friends see it, and you can switch it off on your own profile under Edit profile.

items.title: You is easier to find your way around
items.text: The You tab is now in three clear parts. Your watching comes first: History, Ratings and Liked as big tiles that show how many you have, with Lilin Wrapped right under them. Then People (Friends, with their faces, and Moments), and then your settings. Every row has its own icon, and your numbers sit on your card at the top.

items.title: Only 5 stars counts as a like
items.text: Giving a film or show stars only adds a thumbs up when it's a full 5 stars. With 2½ to 4½ stars you can still like it yourself; only ½ to 2 stars and a like don't go together (that's a thumbs down). Likes that 3½ to 4½ stars gave earlier have been taken back (your stars stay), so your Liked list shows what you really loved. The same goes for likes that came over from Letterboxd stars under 5; Letterboxd hearts stay likes.

items.title: No more blurry season packs
items.text: When a show downloads a whole season, it no longer takes a tiny “1080p” copy that is far too small to look sharp while a proper one is out there. Only if nothing better exists does the small one still come.

title: Discover gets into the holiday spirit

items.title: A holiday row on Discover
items.text: In the weeks before Christmas, New Year’s Eve, Valentine’s Day and Halloween, Discover gets a row for the holiday near the top. Christmas is on now.

items.title: For you leans toward the season
items.text: During a holiday, For you also mixes in a few holiday films and shows that suit what you usually watch.

items.title: Three new moods
items.text: Halloween night, New Year’s Eve and Valentine’s date night join Snowed-in Christmas in Moods, each in its own season.

items.title: My list
items.text: Save for later and Follow are now one button: My list. Everything on your list shows up on Discover, right under Continue watching, with when it’s out or how it’s doing.

items.title: Your list downloads by itself
items.text: Add a film and Lilin gets a good copy as soon as one is out, never a cinema recording. Add a show and it gets the season you’re up to, then each new episode as it airs. You get a notification when it’s ready to watch (switch it off in You, under Notifications).

items.title: Your saved and followed titles moved over
items.text: Everything you had saved or followed is on My list now.

items.title: Remove searches you don’t want to see again
items.text: Each recent search in Search now has a small ×. Tap it to remove that search from the list.

items.title: Find a film or show from what you remember
items.text: Can’t remember the name? Type what you do remember in Search, like “teacher makes meth with his student”, and tap MAGIc search. It looks through the plots of films and shows on Wikipedia, new ones too, and lists the best fits with the words that matched.

items.title: Subtitles stay complete after a download is tidied up
items.text: An episode watched with Play now could keep only its first few subtitle lines after Lilin finished and tidied up the download. Lilin now reads the full subtitles from the copy it keeps, so the whole episode has them.

items.title: Full subtitles during Play now
items.text: Some episodes started with only the first few subtitle lines while they were still downloading, and the rest never came. Lilin now keeps reading the subtitles from the video as it arrives, so the whole episode gets them, on the TV too (restart the TV app once).

items.title: Skip the “Previously on” recap
items.text: When an episode opens with a recap of earlier episodes, the Skip intro button now says Skip recap and jumps past it. Lilin finds recaps by listening for scenes from the episode or two before, so it works on the phone, the computer and the TV (restart the TV app once). Recaps are never skipped on their own, even if you skip intros automatically. In shows you already have, the button can take until the next episode to turn up.

title: The TV picks the right episode

items.title: Shows on the TV continue from your latest episode
items.text: On the TV, a show could open on an older episode you once stopped near the end, instead of the episode after the one you just finished. It now always picks up from what you watched most recently (restart the TV app once).

items.title: Stopping at the credits marks the episode watched
items.text: If you closed the player or the app while the credits played and Next episode was showing, the episode stayed in Continue watching as unfinished. It now counts as watched, and the next episode shows up in Continue watching instead. Works on the website and the TV app (restart the TV app once).

items.title: Shows list every season on the TV
items.text: On the TV, a show you already had a few seasons of only listed those seasons. It now opens on the full page with every season, and any episode plays: ones you have start right away, the rest get ready first.

title: All subtitle lines on Samsung TVs

items.title: Long subtitle lines show up on the TV
items.text: On Samsung TVs, longer subtitle lines could stay blank while short ones showed, which hit Swedish subtitles the most. Every line shows now. Restart the TV app once to get the fix.

items.title: The credits keep playing in the small picture
items.text: On Samsung TVs, the small picture next to the end credits card was black. It now shows the credits as they roll. Restart the TV app once to get the fix.

items.title: Who's watching? on the TV app
items.text: One TV can now keep several people signed in. When the TV app starts it asks who's watching, so Continue watching, your list and what you've seen are your own. Add someone with Add profile (scan the code with their phone), switch with Switch profile on the top bar, and remove one under Manage profiles.

title: The credits card, on every show

items.title: Next episode starts with the credits song
items.text: On shows where the end credits change every episode, the credits card now shows when the closing song starts, with the usual 10 second countdown to the next episode. Before, it waited until the song was over and only showed a button.

items.title: Next episode shows up even when the subtitles arrive late
items.text: On shows where the end credits change every episode, Next episode could go missing when an episode's subtitles were still downloading as you pressed play. The player now checks again while you watch, on the TV app too.

items.title: Anime get their English dub as an audio track
items.text: There's no Dubbed choice to make any more. When you add an anime, Lilin also looks for its English dub and adds it to the episodes you already have, lined up with the picture. Switch between Japanese and English under Audio in the player. If a dub isn't out yet, Lilin checks again every week for a while.

items.title: Next episode shows up when the credits start
items.text: Some shows use different music over the credits every episode, so Lilin couldn't tell where they began and only offered the next episode at the very end. Now it also looks at where the talking stops and shows the Next episode button there. It won't start playing on its own until the credits are over.

items.title: Subtitles from the video itself come first
items.text: Many videos come with their own subtitles, made for exactly that copy. Lilin now always uses those before downloading any, even while a video is still downloading: lines keep appearing as more of it arrives.

items.title: Out-of-sync subtitles get swapped
items.text: Downloaded subtitles are sometimes made for a different cut, with scenes in another order. When Lilin can’t line them up, it now tries other subtitles for the same episode or film and keeps the first that fits. Subtitles picked while a video was still downloading are also checked once it’s done.

items.title: Find any setting by typing
items.text: There’s a search box at the top of You. Type a word like “subtitles” or “notifications” and Lilin shows every page and setting that matches, with where it lives. Tap one and Lilin opens that page, scrolls to the setting and lights it up for a moment.

items.title: The episode you press Play on downloads first
items.text: Lilin downloads a show’s episodes one at a time, in order. If you pressed Play on a later episode before the earlier ones were done, it could sit at “Almost ready” waiting its turn. Now the episode you play starts right away, and the ones after it come next.

items.title: Newer anime seasons are found again
items.text: JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure: Steel Ball Run said it couldn’t find a good copy, even though plenty are out. Lilin now searches for it under the names the uploads actually use, and the same fix helps other anime whose newest season is split into parts.

items.title: English subtitles show every line again
items.text: Some anime (Dandadan, Overlord, Frieren, Mushoku Tensei and a few more) only showed the odd sign on screen when you turned on English subtitles, because Lilin picked the signs-only track. They now use the full subtitles, and new downloads skip signs-only tracks.

items.title: Lilin checks your connection first
items.text: Before a video starts, Lilin quickly tests how fast your connection to the server is. If the 4K copy is too big for it, you get a lighter version of the film instead, or a lighter stream made live from it, so it plays without stopping. On a fast connection nothing changes. You can still pick a version yourself under Quality.

items.title: A dead copy isn't tried twice
items.text: When the copy Lilin picked for a show never starts, it now really looks for a different one instead of trying the same dead copy again.

items.title: Fewer popup messages
items.text: Lilin no longer pops up a message for things you can already see, like the quality it's playing, where it resumed, or that something was saved. Errors, Undo and real tips still show.

items.title: Messages match your theme
items.text: The messages that are left are dark glass in your theme's colours instead of a bright white bubble.

items.title: No more little confirmation popups
items.text: The small white messages that popped up after almost everything you did are gone. Only the one with an Undo button still shows, so you can take back a delete.

title: Up next while the next episode is getting ready

items.title: Up next shows up even if the next episode is still getting ready
items.text: When the next episode was still being made ready for your browser, the Up next prompt didn't appear at the end of an episode. Now it does, and the next episode starts right away in 1080p until the full-quality version is ready.

items.title: Next episode marks the episode watched
items.text: Pressing Next episode during the credits now marks the episode you were on as watched, instead of saving your spot at the credits. It no longer hangs around in Continue watching with an almost full bar.

items.title: Play and Next episode are white again
items.text: The text on Play buttons and on the Next episode countdown in the player is white again on the new red, so it's easier to read.

items.title: More to browse in Anime
items.text: The Anime tab now has rows for Shōnen, Seinen, Shōjo, Josei and Isekai, plus Dark fantasy, Slice of life, Romance, Sports, Mecha, Psychological, Supernatural, Iyashikei, Magical girls, Idols, Cyberpunk, Martial arts, Time travel and School life. The best-known series come first, and See all opens the whole list.

items.title: The reload notice waits until you stop watching
items.text: When Lilin gets updated while you're watching, the "Lilin was updated, reload the page" notice no longer pops up over the video. It waits until the player is closed.

items.title: An Anime tab in Discover
items.text: Discover has an Anime tab next to Films, Shows and Documentaries: popular anime, this season's new shows, new episodes this week, anime films and the top rated. Genres works there too.

items.title: Every title page shows its rating
items.text: Shows opened from Continue watching or New episodes, and titles opened from someone's list, now show their ★ rating like everything else.

items.title: See all likes on a profile
items.text: The Liked row on a profile now has a See all button. It opens every title they liked as a grid, and Show less folds it back.

items.title: Shared clips play on slower connections
items.text: Shared clips now also come in a lighter 1080p version. It plays on screens that are 1080p or smaller, and the clip switches to it by itself if the full-quality version keeps stopping to load.

title: Letterboxd films land on the right title

items.title: No more look-alike films from Letterboxd
items.text: When two films share a name and year, a Letterboxd import could pick the wrong one (like a short film instead of the feature) and show the watch twice. Lilin now uses the exact film Letterboxd points to, fixes earlier mix-ups by itself and shows each watch once.

title: Discover scrolls smoothly late at night

items.title: Smooth scrolling after midnight
items.text: Between midnight and 5 am, Discover scrolled in jerks in Firefox. The late-night look is the same, it just no longer slows the page down.

title: Both TV apps in the new look, and now the same app

items.title: TV apps in Lilin's new look
items.text: The Samsung and Android TV apps have Lilin's new colours, logo and app icon. They also follow the theme you picked in Settings → Appearance, light themes included.

items.title: Android TV runs the Samsung app
items.text: The Android TV app now runs the same app as Samsung TVs, so the two look and work the same: the redesigned title pages with cast and More like this, smoother scrolling and the same player. The app updates itself to version 2.3.0; open Lilin once to get it.

items.title: Watched episodes on the TV
items.text: A show's episode row on the TV ticks off the episodes you've finished, on any device.

items.title: Credits card on the TV
items.text: When the credits roll on the TV, the show's picture fills the screen around the small video, with its logo and what the next episode is about.

title: The tab icon wears your theme

items.title: Tab icon in your colours
items.text: The little Lilin icon on your browser tab now takes the colours of the theme you picked in Appearance.

title: New episodes listens to your library

items.title: Removed shows leave New episodes
items.text: A show you removed from your library no longer shows up under New episodes on Discover. Shows you follow still do.

items.title: Cleaner You tab on phones
items.text: When you're on You, the ring around your picture shows it. The little light above the tab is gone there; the other tabs keep it.

items.title: New Lilin colours
items.text: The Lilin theme is now deep ink with bone-white text and a signal-red light, taken from the new billboard. If you picked another theme in Settings → Appearance, you keep it.

items.title: Two new themes: Dusk and Bone
items.text: Dusk is the billboard's purple evening sky, and Bone is a light theme in the same colours. Find them in Settings → Appearance.

items.title: New logo and app icon
items.text: The header has the new LiLiN wordmark, and the app icon is a black LN monogram on signal red. A phone may keep the old Home Screen icon until you add Lilin again.

title: Shared lists look good in chats

items.title: List links show their posters
items.text: When you share a list and paste the link in Discord or another chat, the preview shows the list's name and a row of its first posters. Private lists show nothing about themselves.

items.title: A new Lilin link picture
items.text: Links to Lilin itself, invites and watch rooms without artwork now show the new Lilin billboard.

title: Phones: watch from your Home Screen

items.title: A nudge to add Lilin to your Home Screen
items.text: When you play something on a phone in the browser, Lilin shows how to add it to your Home Screen. From there it opens like an app: no browser bars and the video fills the screen. Tap Not now to be reminded in a week, or Don't show again.

items.title: Watched episodes are ticked off
items.text: On a show's page, every episode you've finished gets a tick and says Watched, so you can see at a glance where you are.

items.title: Edit profile in four tabs
items.text: Edit profile is split into Profile, Favourites, Look and Page instead of one long list, and the text fields are easier to read and tap.

items.title: See your profile while you edit it
items.text: A small card at the top shows your banner, picture, name, pronouns and colour, and changes as you type or pick a new look.

items.title: Diary folds each show into one line
items.text: A show you watch over several days now takes one line per month in a diary, with the days and the episodes as a range (like S1 E1–8). Tap the arrow to see each day.

items.title: Films or shows only in the diary
items.text: All, Films and Shows above the diary pick what it lists. Your choice is kept on this device.

items.title: Add works on copy-protected SVT Play titles
items.text: Some shows on SVT Play, like The Terror, are copy protected, so they can't be saved from there. Pressing Add on one used to stop at "Needs attention". Now Lilin gets it from the usual sources instead, and the failed SVT copies leave your downloads.

items.title: Sign-in and invite pages tidied up
items.text: The sign-in page and the invite page now carry the new Lilin logo, each label sits with its box, the boxes have small icons, and an eye button shows the password you typed so you can check it. On a computer, the scan-with-your-phone code sits in its own panel next to the password form.

items.title: Back to Discover keeps your place
items.text: Open a mood, a genre or See all and go back, and Discover puts you where you were: just as far down the page, and just as far along the Moods row and the other rows.

items.title: Moods open the right genre
items.text: Into the unknown opened Action instead of Adventure, and Out of this world could open Fantasy instead of Science Fiction. They now open their own genre.

items.title: A new look for Lilin
items.text: Lilin has a new logo: the name set like a film title, with the dots of its two i's as lit bulbs. You'll see it at the top of the app, on its icon (add it to your Home Screen again to get the new one), on the TV apps and on the picture people see when you send them a link or an invite.

items.title: The credits card shows the show and what's next
items.text: When the closing credits start, the screen now fills with a big, sharp picture from the show, with its logo, and Up next tells you what the next episode is about, how long it is and when it aired.

title: Continue watching keeps the episode you just reached

items.title: Shows no longer vanish from Continue watching
items.text: If you once started an episode from a later season and stopped, that old episode could replace the one you'd just reached with Next episode, and the show could vanish from Continue watching. It now shows the episode you're really on.

title: Credits card and 4K switch on the TVs

items.title: The credits card on the TV
items.text: When the closing credits start, the picture moves to the right and the TV shows the song from the soundtrack and what's up next, like the website. Press Up for the picture full size again.

items.title: The TV moves to 4K by itself
items.text: When a film starts on a quick 1080p copy and the 4K version finishes downloading while you watch, the TV switches to it at the same spot, once per film. Android TVs update themselves to show the credits card with the picture on the side.

title: Steadier TV apps on slow connections

items.title: No more Reconnecting loops on Android TV
items.text: On a slow or uneven connection (watching from far away, for example) the Android TV app used to stop and reconnect over and over. It now keeps playing the full-quality file while the connection keeps up, and if it can't, it moves once to a stream that adjusts its quality to the connection by itself. The Android TV app updates itself to get this.

items.title: Autoplay switch on the TVs
items.text: Press Down while an episode plays: Autoplay next episode can be turned off, like on the website. Up next then waits for you.

items.title: Subtitles and sharp frames on the TVs
items.text: Videos you start while they're still downloading get subtitles on the TV too, and Continue watching shows a sharp frame from where you stopped.

items.title: A credits card when the credits roll
items.text: When the closing credits start, the picture slides into a corner and a card shows the song from the soundtrack (with a link to Spotify or YouTube Music) and what's up next. It says how sure it is: a track named for the end credits, the show's theme, or just from the soundtrack. Tap the small picture or Back to the picture to watch the credits full size.

items.title: Discover changes with the time of day
items.text: In the morning Discover gets a warmer glow and a row of short, bright picks. After midnight it goes dark, with a Late night row of strange films under 95 minutes. It goes by the clock on your device.

items.title: Channel static on Live TV
items.text: Switching channels now gives a short burst of static and the channel number in the corner, like an old TV.

title: Full quality waits for its sound

items.title: No more waiting after Switch now
items.text: When something you're watching finishes downloading, Full quality is ready only shows up once its sound plays in your browser. Before, you could switch and then sit through Adding normal stereo sound; now the stream keeps playing until the switch is instant.

title: Lists, ticket stubs and ghost reactions

items.title: Ghost reactions
items.text: Tap the smiley in the player to leave an emoji at that exact moment. When a friend watches the same film or episode later, it pops up at that second, like "ebi 💀 41:12". The seek bar shows small dots where friends reacted. You can turn friends’ reactions off from the same smiley.

items.title: Lists
items.text: Put films and shows together in lists, like "films that ruined my sleep". Tap List next to the thumbs on any title page, number them if it’s a ranking, and share the link. Lists show on your profile for the people who can see it, or keep one just for you.

items.title: Ticket stubs in your diary
items.text: Every film in your profile’s diary is now a little torn ticket stub in the poster’s colour, with the day, the time you watched it and its number in your film history.

items.title: Subtitles in Play now
items.text: Watching something while it downloads now has subtitles too. Pick a language like usual and it stays on when the finished file takes over.

items.title: Episode names in Play now
items.text: Watching an episode while it downloads now shows its name in the player, like "Season 1, Episode 1: A Shadow of the Past", not just the season and episode number.

items.title: Turn off autoplay for the next episode
items.text: The settings cog in the player has a new Autoplay next episode switch. Turn it off and the Up next card still shows at the end of an episode, but it waits for you instead of counting down. It's remembered on each device.

items.title: Machines right on the House page
items.text: The machine status bar at the top of House is gone. Everything that was behind it (the server, VPN, sharing, power and every machine) now sits right on the House page, under the other buttons.

items.title: Continue watching pictures are sharp now
items.text: The picture on each Continue watching card, the moment where you stopped, used to be a tiny blurry thumbnail stretched to fit. It's now a full-quality frame from the video, so it looks crisp on iPads and big screens too.

title: Subtitles in fullscreen on iPad and iPhone

items.title: Two-line subtitles in the right order
items.text: In the iPad and iPhone fullscreen player, some shows put the first line of a two-line subtitle underneath the second, so it read backwards. The lines now stay in order there too.

items.title: Films with a different year now download
items.text: Some films said no release matched even though copies existed, because the uploads use the premiere year while Lilin knew the later cinema year (Clean, Shaven: 1993 vs 1995). Lilin now accepts those copies when nothing closer exists.

items.title: No more blank twins in search
items.text: Some films showed up twice in search, and the second one was empty when you opened it: a blank copy someone added to the film database. Lilin now hides those.

items.title: The fullscreen button is back on iPad
items.text: In the Lilin app on an iPad's Home Screen the fullscreen button was missing. It's back: tap it to watch in iPad's own player, which hides the clock and battery at the top. Close it and you're back in Lilin's player where you left off.

items.title: Languages and subtitle settings side by side
items.text: The subtitle menu is wider now. Languages are on the left and scroll on their own, and the size, style, height, second language and timing are on the right, so you don't have to scroll past every language to reach them. On narrow phones the two halves stack.

items.title: Subtitles, audio, night mode and quality under one cog
items.text: The player bar has fewer buttons now. Press the cog to change subtitles, the audio language, night mode and the sleep timer, or the quality. Each one shows what it's set to, and Settings at the top of each list takes you back.

items.title: Clip a moment has its own button
items.text: The scissors next to the cog start Clip a moment straight away, instead of hiding it in the ⋯ menu.

items.title: No clock or battery over the video on iPad
items.text: In the Lilin app on your iPad Home Screen, videos now open fullscreen, so the time and battery at the top are gone while you watch. Swipe down or press the fullscreen button to leave it.

items.title: A dual-boot PC in Windows shows as on
items.text: When a dual-boot computer is running Windows, its card in the House tab now says On · Windows instead of Off, or in Windows, and its health shows up too. Restart and Restart into Linux work from Windows as well, and a plain restart comes back to Windows. The Windows PC needs the new Windows helper (agents/lilin-house-windows.py) set up once.

title: Episodes on the TV show page

items.title: Pick an episode right on the TV
items.text: On a show's page on the TV, move along the seasons and that season's episodes show right underneath. Press down, scroll through them sideways and press the one you want to watch. The Play season and Episodes buttons are gone, and the wrong season no longer opens. Samsung TVs: restart the app to see it.

title: A nicer wait on the TV

items.title: The title fills in on the TV too
items.text: When something is getting ready to play on the Android TV or Samsung TV app, its title art fills in with colour as it loads, the same as on your phone and computer. Restart the TV app to see it.

items.title: Roomier title pages on Samsung TVs
items.text: Film and show pages on the Samsung TV app have more room to breathe: the whole description, running time and age rating, the cast with their photos, and a More like this row. Press down from Play to scroll through them. Restart the TV app to see it.

items.title: No more Go to library on the TV
items.text: The TV apps have no library page, so the leftover Go to library buttons are gone. On SVT Play pages, Add to library is now Save, and something that's on its way just says so.

items.title: No Download button on the TV
items.text: The TV apps no longer show Download or Quality on a title's page. Play still gets anything ready to watch; start downloads from the website.

items.title: Your colours on the TV
items.text: The TV app now uses the colour theme you picked in Settings → Appearance. Restart the TV app to see it.

items.title: No more endless Reconnecting
items.text: On a slower connection, the TV app could keep restarting a film while it was still loading and show Reconnecting for minutes. It now gives the film time to load, and if it keeps stalling it switches to a lighter 720p stream so it keeps playing.

items.title: The TV plays your best copy
items.text: When a title has several copies, the TV app now plays the best one your TV can show, like the 4K version on a 4K TV, instead of whichever came first.

items.title: Cinema recordings are caught
items.text: Some copies filmed in a cinema were labelled as normal web releases and got picked. Lilin now recognises them, and picks a proper copy instead whenever one exists.

items.title: A warning on the TV before Play
items.text: When a new film only exists as cinema recordings so far, the TV says so under Play. Pressing Play asks first, and you can still watch the recording if you want to.

title: Removing from Continue watching really works

items.title: Removed titles stay removed
items.text: Remove from Continue watching didn’t save, so the title came back when you reloaded. It saves now and stays gone on all your devices until you watch it again. Sign out everywhere on the Account page works again too.

items.title: Press Play on anything
items.text: On the Samsung and Android TV apps, every film and show in Discover and Search has a Play button now. If it isn’t on Lilin yet, the TV shows Getting it ready while Lilin finds a copy, and it starts playing by itself as soon as the start of the video is here. Pressing Back lets it keep getting ready.

items.title: The TV opens on Discover
items.text: The TV apps no longer have a library screen. They open on Discover, with Continue watching at the top and Live TV in the bar.

items.title: The next episode follows
items.text: When an episode ends, Up next offers the next one even if it isn’t on Lilin yet. Continue watching on the TV now shows the episode after the one you finished, one card per show.

items.title: Moods on the TV
items.text: Discover on the TV has the Moods row too. Pick one to see everything that fits it.

items.title: A pause screen on the TV
items.text: Pause for a few seconds and the picture dims, with the title, the episode and how much is left. Press any button to bring the controls back.

items.title: Live TV chat on the TV
items.text: Messages from a channel’s chat show up at the side of the screen while you watch Live TV on the TV, and fade after a few seconds. Turn them off with Down, then Chat.

items.title: No more Quality setting
items.text: Lilin now picks the picture for the screen you’re watching on. On a 1080p screen, films come in 1080p. Phones get 1080p too: at that size 4K looks no sharper. On a TV or a 1440p or 4K monitor, a film starts in 1080p so it plays quickly, the 4K version downloads in the background, and playback moves to it once it’s ready.

items.title: Get a sharper copy
items.text: Watching a film that’s only here in 1080p on a sharper screen? Open Quality in the player and press Get a sharper copy. The 4K version downloads in the background and playback moves to it when it’s done.

items.title: No more question-mark posters
items.text: On iPhones, some posters on Discover showed an empty box with a question mark instead of the picture. They load normally again.

items.title: Tabs for New, Improved and Fixes
items.text: The What’s new list now has tabs at the top, so you can see just the new features, just the improvements or just the bug fixes. Each note’s dot shows its kind too: gold for new, blue for improved, green for fixes.

items.title: Speaker no longer hides under Trailer
items.text: On shows with both a theme song and a trailer, the small speaker now sits just above the Trailer button, so you can reach it.

items.title: Title pages take on the film’s colour
items.text: Each title page picks up the main colour of its picture, now in the Play button’s glow too, and remembers it so it’s there right away next time.

items.title: A pause screen
items.text: Pause for a few seconds and the picture dims while the title, episode and a short description fade in. Touch anything to make it go away.

items.title: Continue watching shows where you stopped
items.text: Cards in Continue watching show the actual frame where you left off, when Lilin has one.

items.title: Smoother loading
items.text: Posters fade in from their own colour instead of grey boxes popping in, and rows fade out softly at the edges when there’s more to scroll.

items.title: Up next fills in
items.text: During the Up next countdown, the next episode’s picture fills in with colour, like the logo on Getting it ready.

items.title: Live TV feels like TV
items.text: Switching channels cuts to black for a moment, then the channel and what’s on now slide in.

title: New films start faster, then sharpen

items.title: Starts in 1080p, switches to 4K by itself
items.text: A film that isn’t on the server yet now starts from a quick 1080p copy. The 4K copy downloads in the background, and when it’s ready your film moves over to it at the same spot, on screens sharp enough to show the difference.

items.title: An honest wait
items.text: While the very start of a video is still on its way, Getting it ready no longer shows a countdown that doesn’t move.

title: Videos you haven’t watched before start smoother

items.title: Copies wait while your video starts
items.text: While a video that isn’t on the server yet is getting ready, Lilin now pauses its own background work (making copies for later) so your video gets the graphics card and the disk to itself. The paused work carries on once playback is going.

title: Removed from Continue watching stays removed

items.title: Removing a title takes it off everywhere
items.text: Remove from Continue watching now works for the whole show, so an older episode you half watched no longer pops up in its place. It is also removed on all your devices, not just the one you used. Watching it again brings it back.

title: Depth on the big picture on phones

items.title: The Discover picture sinks as you scroll
items.text: On phones the big picture at the top of Discover now slides away slower than the rows, so they glide over it, like on a computer.

items.title: The big search field on Discover is gone
items.text: Phones showed two ways to search at the top of Discover. Now there is just the magnifying glass in the top corner, so the picture has more room.

items.title: Films that need a version for your browser start right away
items.text: If your browser needed Lilin to make a version of a film, it could sit on "Waiting to start" for hours while episodes other people were about to watch were being prepared. Now the film you pressed Play on always goes first.

items.title: Watch while it's being made
items.text: When your browser can't play a film's picture, it now starts right away in 1080p while the full-quality version is made, and switches over by itself when that's ready.

items.title: The title fills in while it gets ready
items.text: When a film or episode is getting ready to play, its title art now sits in the middle of the screen and fills in with colour as it loads, so you can see how far along it is.

items.title: Right now is gone
items.text: The Right now strip at the top of Discover is gone, so Discover starts with what to watch. Your Wrapped is still in You.

items.title: No more Library
items.text: Find something on Discover or in search and press Play. That's all there is to it now: no adding, no waiting for downloads, no list to keep tidy. The Library tab is gone, and the tabs are Discover, Live and You.

items.title: Getting it ready
items.text: When a film or episode isn't on Lilin yet, Play opens the player straight away and says what's happening, like "Starting in about 30 s". It starts playing by itself when it's ready, usually within a minute. Cancel if you change your mind.

items.title: The lightning mark plays at once
items.text: Titles with a small lightning mark are already here and start instantly. Tap Instant on Discover to see only those.

items.title: Your things are on Discover
items.text: Continue watching, new episodes of shows you watch, and anything you've saved for later now sit at the top of Discover. Pressing an episode plays it, and the next ones come along by themselves.

items.title: No more waiting on one slow piece
items.text: A video you watch for the first time sometimes took minutes to start while one small part of it came from a single slow source. Lilin now fetches that part from other sources at the same time, and starts most videos without waiting for the very end of the file.

items.title: A dead copy gets replaced
items.text: If the copy Lilin picked never starts downloading at all, it now tries another one by itself after about a minute instead of waiting for ever.

items.title: Episodes of older shows play too
items.text: Many episodes, mostly of older shows like Friends, only exist inside a download of the whole season. Press one of them now and Lilin gets just that episode first and starts it, then the episodes after it follow in order. Before, it said it couldn't find a good copy. Shows with an apostrophe in the name, like Grey's Anatomy, are found now too.

items.title: Best Quality starts quickly
items.text: With Best Quality on, a film you haven't watched before now starts from a copy that can play while it downloads, instead of a huge one that never got ready. The best copy follows in the background and shows up as another version you can switch to.

items.title: Subtitles show once
items.text: Moments with subtitles showed them twice on iPhone. Now there's just the one line, right under the picture.

items.title: Rate in half stars
items.text: Tap the left half of a star to give half a star, so 3½ is finally an option. Profiles show them like ★★★½, and Letterboxd ratings come over exactly as you gave them. 3½ stars and up counts as a thumbs up.

items.title: Link your Letterboxd account
items.text: Edit profile → Letterboxd: type your Letterboxd username and what you log there shows up on your Lilin profile. Films land in your diary, and your stars and reviews show on the title pages. Lilin checks for new ones every few hours. Anything you rated or reviewed in Lilin yourself stays as you left it.

items.title: Your whole history and top four
items.text: Letterboxd only shares your newest entries this way. For everything, export your data on letterboxd.com (Settings → Data) and pick the zip in the same place. It brings your full diary, ratings, reviews and your four favourites.

title: Things that aren't here yet start sooner

items.title: Play now in seconds, not minutes
items.text: When you download a film or an episode, Lilin now gets it ready to watch straight away: the start of the video comes first, so Play now shows up sooner and starts right after you press it. If the copy Lilin picked turns out slow, dead or fake, it switches to a better one on its own, and searches are quicker too.

items.title: The next episodes follow
items.text: Download one episode and, once it plays smoothly, the episodes after it in that season come too, so you can keep watching.

items.title: See where you're signed in
items.text: You → Account now lists the browsers and TVs signed in as you. Lost a phone? Sign out everywhere else, and every other device needs your password to get back in. Changing your password does the same.

title: Titles in Continue watching open the page

items.title: Tap the name to see the show or film
items.text: In Continue watching, tapping the picture still picks up where you stopped. Tapping the name under it now opens the title's page instead, with its seasons, details and trailer. The ⋯ menu has a Details button too.

title: Sign in by scanning a code

items.title: No password on computers and TVs
items.text: The sign-in page on a computer and the sign-in screen on the TV now show a QR code. Point the camera of a phone that's signed in to Lilin at it, check that it names the right device, and say yes. No camera? Enter the code under You → Devices and notifications instead.

items.title: Better pictures at the top of Discover
items.text: The big banner now picks a well-liked, full-HD-or-better picture without text for each title instead of whatever the movie database lists first, and big screens get the full-size picture instead of a stretched one.

items.title: Activity is a House tile now
items.text: Who watched what, and when, now opens from the House tab next to your other tools instead of from You. Old links still find it.

title: Just-downloaded films get ready in more browsers

items.title: No more "can't play" right after a download
items.text: Some new films use a video format a few browsers (like Firefox) can't play. Right after the download, Lilin used to just say it can't play here. Now it shows that it's making a version for your browser and starts by itself when that's ready.

items.title: A note where you pick your password
items.text: When you join Lilin or pick a password, a small note now says what was always true: your password is scrambled before it's saved, so nobody can see it, not even the people who run Lilin.

items.title: Four tabs: Discover, Live, Library and You
items.text: Lilin has gained a lot of features lately, so everything got a clearer home. The tabs are now Discover, Live, Library and You. Settings moved into You, together with your profile, friends, moments and what you've watched. Owners have all their tools in one tab, House.

items.title: Library in three parts
items.text: Library now has Titles, Watchlist and Downloads. Watchlist is one list for what you saved for later, what's coming up and the shows you follow. Downloads has everything about what's on its way.

items.title: A shorter Discover with Right now
items.text: Discover is shorter. Right under the big picture, Right now shows what needs you today: a watch party, something leaving soon or a download that's ready.

items.title: Watch with someone on Live
items.text: Live has a new Watch with someone section at the top: start Pick together, or join the watch parties you planned.

items.title: One title page, one way to invite, smarter search
items.text: Every film and show opens the same page, with one main button for what you'll most likely do next. Inviting people works the same everywhere. Search also finds places and settings, so typing "subtitles" takes you straight there.

items.title: Show pages play their theme song
items.text: Open a show in your Library and its theme song plays quietly in the background, like the menu of a home cinema. It keeps going while you look through seasons and episodes, and fades out when you press play or leave the page. Tap the small speaker on the picture to stop it. Turn it off, or a little louder, on each device in Settings → Watching → Theme music. Shows where Lilin hasn’t found the opening titles yet stay silent.

title: Profiles stay put, clips arrive by themselves

items.title: Reloading keeps your profile open
items.text: Reloading the page while a profile is open now brings you back to that profile, even after you've edited it or opened a film from it. Before, you landed in Settings.

items.title: New clips appear on their own
items.text: The Clips tab now updates by itself when a new clip arrives, so there's no need to reload to see it.

items.title: Whole Liked row on computers
items.text: On a computer, the Liked row on a profile now shows every poster in a tidy grid, so nothing is cut off at the edge and there's nothing to scroll.

items.title: Name and picture on your profile
items.text: Change your picture by tapping it on your profile, and your name under Edit profile. Settings is shorter: the picture, name and What's new rows are gone from the top.

items.title: Save stays out of the way
items.text: The Save button in Edit profile now sits on its own bar at the bottom of the sheet, so the poster and font choices no longer show through around it.

items.title: Tidier bio box
items.text: The Bio field on your profile is now a normal rounded box instead of a stretched pill, so longer bios no longer run into the curved edges.

items.title: No Add on films that aren't out yet
items.text: Films that are only in cinemas and shows that haven't started airing no longer offer Add to library on their cards. Save or Follow them instead, and Lilin adds them once they're out.

items.title: Watch Together fits the screen
items.text: On phones and upright tablets the room now sits under the picture instead of covering it, and turned sideways it docks on the right and leaves the controls free. The Audio button is back in rooms, so everyone can pick their own audio language.

items.title: A calmer player
items.text: Only one player menu opens at a time, and Escape or a tap outside closes it. When a video can't play you get a clear card with Try again and Back, and if the connection drops mid-video the player reconnects by itself.

items.title: Easier to read
items.text: Buttons, status colours and the current tab are easier to read on every colour theme, light ones included. SVT Play titles are readable over their picture, and ratings look the same everywhere.

items.title: Plain words when something's wrong
items.text: If Lilin can't be reached you get a clear message and a Try again button instead of technical words. A link that got cut off when it was sent now shows a page saying so, and invite and Watch Together links are in Swedish too.

items.title: Your library tells the truth
items.text: A show that's still downloading no longer says you're all caught up, episodes that haven't aired yet show their air date, films with several versions let you pick the quality on their library page, and an empty filtered library has a Show all titles button.

items.title: Restricted means restricted
items.text: People who are restricted no longer show up for anyone else in Live TV, Watch Together or the live chat, on any of their devices.

items.title: Opens faster
items.text: After the first visit Lilin reuses what it already downloaded, and what it does download is smaller, so it opens quicker on a slow connection.

items.title: A page that's yours
items.text: Tap your face at the top (or Your profile in Settings) to see your profile: picture, name, a username, pronouns and a short bio, your four favourite films or shows, what you watched lately with your stars and likes, your reviews and your friends. More activity opens your whole diary.

items.title: Make it look like you
items.text: Edit profile lets you pick an accent colour, a banner (a picture from a film or show, or a colour), the font of your name, the shape of the posters, the background and the layout, and which sections show in which order. You see each change behind the editor before you save.

items.title: You decide who sees it
items.text: Profiles are for friends only until you change it: pick Everyone, Friends or Only me. Others just see your name and picture. Tap someone's face on a review or in your friends list to visit theirs.

items.title: Shows from season packs get their posters
items.text: Some season packs keep their episodes in a folder called something like The Mindy Project Season 1 S01. Lilin read that as a show named The Mindy Project Season 1, couldn’t find it, and showed plain grey tiles called Episode 1, Episode 2 and so on. Those shows now get their poster, episode names and pictures.

items.title: Swipe until you all agree
items.text: Can’t agree on tonight’s film? On Discover, under Moods, tap Can’t agree on what to watch? Choose films or shows, a genre and how long it may be, invite the others (or copy a link) and start. Everyone swipes through the same posters: right for yes, left for no. The posters come from what each of you likes to watch, not only from what’s on the server, and nothing anyone has already seen. The first one you all say yes to pops up as a match, with Watch together now or later if it’s on the server. Nobody sees how you swiped.

items.title: No more digging in Settings
items.text: When someone asks to be your friend, Lilin now shows it as soon as you open it (or right away if you're already in). Accept or decline right there, or press Later and it asks again tomorrow.

items.title: Write it like a message
items.text: The idea box in Settings has a new look. Pick Idea, Something's off or Other at the top of the note, write, and press Send. Your ideas below show where each one stands (Sent, Planned, Added or Not now) with the owner's answer underneath.

items.title: A tidier inbox
items.text: Settings → Ideas now shows each idea with the sender's face, a status light and Planned / Added / Not now right under it. Answer opens a reply box only when you need it, and the scout's cards got the same cleaner look.

items.title: Tidier Liked by line
items.text: When lots of people like a title, the faces and names now sit on their own line under the thumbs instead of squeezing into a narrow column on your phone.

items.title: Send a bit of a film or episode
items.text: While you watch, tap ⋯ in the player and choose Clip a moment. Drag the two yellow handles to pick up to three minutes, press Preview to check it, then Next. Add a note if you like, pick friends to send it to, or copy a link that anyone can open. Moments friends send you are in Settings → Moments, and with notifications on you hear when one arrives. Links stop working after 30 days, or straight away if you delete the moment.

items.title: Browse by mood
items.text: Discover has a new Moods row right after Trending: tiles like Slow-burn rainy day thriller, 90s indie nostalgia, Cozy and comforting, Mind-bending and Late-night neon. Tap one for a page of films and shows that fit the feeling, with what you already have first. The order changes every day, and Shuffle mixes it up again.

items.title: The right film when two share a name
items.text: Some films share their name and year with another one. In 2026 there were three films called The Odyssey, so uploads of the short ones showed up as Nolan's long before his was out. Lilin now checks how long the video is in the first minutes of a download. If it's clearly the other film of that name, Lilin removes it and looks for the right one. It only steps in when the length matches the other film, so a real copy is never thrown out.

items.title: Who made it, and the music in it
items.text: At the very bottom of every film and show page there's now a folded More details. Open it to see the director, writers, showrunners, composer and the rest of the crew, the studios, countries and release dates, budget and box office, and links to IMDb, Wikipedia and more. When a soundtrack album exists, its songs are listed too: tap one to find it on Spotify or YouTube Music. Episodes in the episode list get a small Credits fold with that episode's director, writers and guest stars. Nothing opens unless you ask for it.

items.title: Talk while you watch a channel
items.text: Channels in Live now have a chat. Press Chat under what's on to open it: beside the picture on a computer or a phone held sideways, under it on a phone held upright. Everyone on the same channel sees what you write, and messages stay with the channel, so whoever tunes in later can read what was said. With the chat closed, new messages pop up briefly over the picture and a dot appears on Chat.

items.title: Rate with stars and write a review
items.text: Next to the thumbs on a film or show there is now a Review button. Give it 1 to 5 stars and, if you like, write what you thought. Everyone on Lilin can read your review, and if it gives something away, tick Contains spoilers so others have to tap to see it. Stars and thumbs go together: 4 or 5 stars counts as a thumbs up, 1 or 2 as a thumbs down.

items.title: See what others thought
items.text: Further down a title's page, Reviews shows the average stars and a couple of reviews. See all opens the rest. You can change or delete your own review whenever you like.

title: An idea scout for the owner

items.title: Ideas with the evidence, in your inbox
items.text: Once a week an agent reads what people have loved or wished for in streaming services over the years and brings the best few to Settings → Ideas, each with links to where people asked for it and how it would fit Lilin. Press Accept (add a comment if you like) and an agent builds it; Comment and the scout answers; Not now puts it aside.

items.title: Activity at a glance
items.text: Activity now opens with today's numbers and everyone who's been around: tap a face to see just what that person did. The feed groups each person's sitting into one card, a run of episodes shows as one line (House S04 E08–E12), subtitles ride along as a small tag, and the buttons at the top show only watching, downloads or library changes.

items.title: Let someone see Activity
items.text: Settings → People has a new Can see activity switch. Whoever you turn it on for gets the Activity tab, read-only: they can't invite or remove anyone, and the other owner tabs stay yours. To invite someone, tap the Invite tile at the start of the people row; tap a person to rename them, send a password link or remove their access.

items.title: See what's coming out
items.text: Discover has a Coming soon row with the films and shows that come out in the next few months: new films in cinemas, films coming to streaming, new series and new seasons. The closest and most talked-about are first, and each card shows the date. See all lists everything by week and month, with Films and Shows to filter.

items.title: Save or follow in one tap
items.text: Each card has a small button to save a film or follow a show right from the row, the same as on the title page. Saved and followed titles show up under Coming up in your Library, and if you can download, Lilin adds them once they're out and sends you a notification.

items.title: Add your friends
items.text: Settings has a new Friends part. Search for someone by name and tap Add: once they say yes, you're friends. Requests you get show up there too, with Accept. With notifications on, you hear when someone asks or says yes. Friends come first when you invite people to Watch Together.

items.title: A Restrict switch in People
items.text: Settings → People has a new Restrict switch for each person. Someone restricted keeps Watch Together, rooms and room chat, but gets none of the other social parts: they don't see who liked what, nobody sees their likes, they can't send or get notification invites, and they share only by copying links.

items.title: The big banner has depth
items.text: When you scroll down Discover, the picture at the top now sinks away slower than the rows, so the rows slide over it. Scrolling also does less work: the small buttons on cards and the glowing dots no longer redraw the page on every frame.

items.title: Tell us what Lilin should do next
items.text: Settings now has an idea box. Write what you wish Lilin did, or something that feels off, and press Send: it goes straight to the owner. Your ideas stay listed under the box, and you see when one is planned or added, plus any answer. With notifications on, you also get a notification when someone answers.

items.title: Volume slider on trailers
items.text: Trailers on a title page now have a volume slider next to the mute button: point at the speaker to show it, or use the up and down arrow keys. Trailers remember the volume you picked. On phones the volume is still your phone's own buttons.

title: Fell asleep? Your place is kept

items.title: Autoplayed episodes don't count as watched
items.text: When episodes play on by themselves and you don't press or tap anything, they no longer count as watched. If you fall asleep, Continue watching picks up at the first episode you missed instead of jumping ahead. Press or tap anything while an episode plays and it counts as normal. Works on the web, the TV app and the Samsung TV app.

title: Continue watching follows your latest episode

items.title: Back where you really stopped
items.text: If you go back to an episode you already finished and stop halfway, Continue watching now picks up that episode again instead of jumping to the one after it. This works across your devices.

title: Rename clips in the clip editor

items.title: Rename while you edit
items.text: The clip's name at the top of the editor is now a button: click it (or press R) to rename the clip without leaving the editor. The header also got a calmer look with room to breathe.

title: More on Live TV, and four new channels

items.title: The channels fill themselves
items.text: Every few hours Live TV now fetches a few popular films and shows by itself, mostly for whichever channel has the least on it: more anime for Anime, more sitcoms for Sitcoms, more films for Films and so on. Shows start from season 1, episode 1.

items.title: New channels
items.text: Drama, Sci-Fi & Fantasy and Action & Adventure join the line-up, plus Fresh, which shows everything new on the server. Series play their episodes in order, with other things in between.

items.title: Live TV on the Samsung TV app
items.text: The Samsung TV app now has Live TV too: pick it in the bar at the top of Home for the guide, then OK to watch. Up and Down (or CH+ and CH−) change channel, numbers go straight to one, Right picks subtitles.

items.title: Like it? Keep it
items.text: These picks aren't in anyone's library. If one hooks you, open it from the channel and press Add to library to keep it. The ones nobody keeps make room for new ones after a while.

title: Pick a show up where you left off

items.title: Play next episode
items.text: A show's page now has one big button that carries on where you are: Resume the episode you're partway through, Play next once you've finished one, or Play S01 E01 if you haven't started. Finished the last one? It says you're all caught up.

items.title: Up next in Continue watching
items.text: When you finish an episode, the next one shows up in Continue watching as Up next, so one tap plays it.

items.title: Your year, on the home screen
items.text: Open Lilin and your Wrapped is waiting at the top of Discover: hours watched, top titles, your show of the year, your genre, your prime time, your biggest binge and who you watched with. It stays there until the end of January, and in Settings after that.

items.title: What kind of watcher were you?
items.text: Wrapped now tells you: Night Owl, Binger, Host, Explorer and more. There's also a slide about everyone's year on Lilin together.

items.title: Share it
items.text: On the last slide, Share your year turns it into a picture for your story or the group chat.

title: Live TV subtitles show up now

items.title: No more vanishing lines
items.text: On a computer, Live TV subtitles slid off the top of the screen whenever the controls were showing. They now sit just above the channel bar.

items.title: Subtitles on the TV's channels
items.text: Watching a channel on the TV app, press Right for subtitles. The language you pick stays on when you change channel or the next programme starts.

items.title: They stay on in the browser too
items.text: On a computer or phone, subtitles you turn on for a channel now come back on the next programme instead of switching off.

items.title: No more "Disc..." in the header
items.text: With Live added, the owner's eight sections got squeezed into cut-off names on computers. They now show in full; on narrower windows the search box gets smaller first.

title: Live TV: channels that are always on

items.title: A Live tab
items.text: Channels made from the library run around the clock: Anime, Sitcoms, Films, Documentaries and your own picks. Open Live for the guide, tap a channel and you're watching whatever is on right now.

items.title: Everyone sees the same moment
items.text: Tune in to the same channel as someone else and you're watching together, on the same frame, with their faces in the corner. No room to set up, nobody has to press Play.

items.title: Surf like it's a TV
items.text: Switch with the arrows in the player, Page Up and Page Down, or type a channel number. On the TV app use Up and Down, the channel buttons, the number keys and the last-channel button.

items.title: Stay with it
items.text: Live TV can't be paused. Watch from start opens the programme in the normal player, and Keep watching carries on from where the channel is and puts it in Continue watching. Just watching a channel leaves Continue watching alone.

title: A wrong password no longer wipes your email

items.title: Only retype the password
items.text: If you mistype your password when signing in, Lilin now keeps the email you typed and puts the cursor straight in the password box.

items.title: House S4 E7 reads normally again
items.text: To fix names in disc subtitles, Lilin borrows the capital letters from a popular subtitle of the same episode. For one House episode that subtitle was written With Every Word Capitalised, and Lilin copied it. Lilin now skips subtitles like that and tries another one.

title: Best Quality picks copies you can watch while they download

items.title: No more crawling 4K downloads
items.text: With Best Quality on, Lilin used to grab the very best copy even when hardly anyone was sharing it, so it downloaded slower than you could watch it. Now it checks first: if the best copy can't keep up with Play now, it picks the best-looking copy that can, usually a 4K web download instead of a huge disc copy. Lilin also watches the first few minutes of each download, and if one turns out too slow, it swaps it for a faster copy by itself (never while you're watching it).

title: Films that aren't out yet say Coming soon

items.title: No more cinema recordings
items.text: Films that are still in cinemas or not released yet (like Avengers: Doomsday) now show a grey Coming soon button instead of Add to library, with the date they come out. Lilin only gets a film once it's out to stream or buy, so you never end up with a blurry recording from a cinema. Press Save and switch on "Add it when a good copy is out" and Lilin adds it by itself on the day.

title: Videos pick up again after a dropped connection

items.title: No more wrong "can't play in this browser" message
items.text: If the connection to Lilin drops while you watch (a Wi-Fi blip or a server restart), the player now says it is reconnecting and carries on from the same spot by itself. Before, it showed a message saying the video couldn't play in your browser, which wasn't true.

title: Play now jumps ahead and stops freezing

items.title: Skip ahead while it downloads
items.text: Play now used to wait for the download to reach the spot you skipped to, which could take minutes. A helper now fetches that part first, so skipping ahead plays again in a couple of seconds. The rest keeps downloading as before.

items.title: No more long freezes
items.text: One slow source could hold back the next part of a video and freeze the picture for a minute or more. The helper now fetches those parts from faster sources. Starting a video is quicker too.

items.title: How it works
items.text: playhead (github.com/Tjabooo/playhead) runs next to qBittorrent, which still downloads, seeds and files everything. It reads what qBittorrent already has from qBittorrent's own file, and fetches only what the player needs next. It's bound to qBittorrent's tunnel address and fenced by the torrent VPN firewall. If anything goes wrong, Play now carries on with qBittorrent alone. PLAY_NOW_ENGINE=qbit turns the helper off.

title: Best Quality stops picking six-hour downloads

items.title: Faster Best Quality picks
items.text: Best Quality used to treat a bigger file as a better one, so it could pick an 80 GB copy with ten people sharing it over a 26 GB copy of the same 4K stream with thousands. Now extra size beyond what a resolution needs barely counts, a huge file with few people sharing it counts against, and copies that may start in a dubbed language (Hindi, Italian and so on) lose out to ones that don't. The picture stays just as good, it just arrives hours sooner.

title: Trailer controls you can actually see

items.title: Normal-sized trailer controls
items.text: Since trailers started playing in full HD, YouTube's own buttons on a title page's trailer were tiny. Trailers now have Lilin's own bar instead: play and pause, a seek bar, mute and full screen, at a normal size. Click the video to pause, double-click for full screen.

title: Used password links tidy themselves up

items.title: Password links leave the list once used
items.text: A password link now disappears from People as soon as that person has a password, however they set it, and it stops working. Making a new password link for someone replaces their old one.

title: Your CS2 moments on the clip timeline

items.title: Kills, deaths and rounds in the clip editor
items.text: CS2 clips now show their kills, headshots, deaths, round starts and ends and bomb plants and defuses as small icons above the editor's timeline. Click one to jump just before it, or press N and P to go to the next or previous one.

title: See how long a copy has left

items.title: Progress bar while a copy is made
items.text: When a video needs a copy before your browser can play it, the player now shows a progress bar with the percentage and roughly how many minutes are left, instead of a line of text.

title: Browser copies keep going through updates

items.title: No more starting over
items.text: Some videos need a copy before your browser can play them (for example HEVC films in Firefox). Every time Lilin was updated, a copy in progress was thrown away and started again from the beginning, so a film could wait for hours. Copies now carry on through an update and finish where they were.

items.title: No more lag in Firefox
items.text: Lilin could feel laggy in Firefox on a computer, worst on pages with a trailer, even on fast PCs. Firefox struggles with the frosted-glass blur behind buttons and menus, so in Firefox those panels are now plain tinted glass instead. Everything else looks the same.

items.title: Sharp, smooth trailers
items.text: Trailers on title pages and behind the Discover banner played in blurry low quality, because YouTube picks the quality from how big the player is and ours were small. They now ask for full HD, and the frosted buttons over a playing banner trailer turn plain so the video doesn't stutter.

items.title: One trailer at a time
items.text: The banner trailer kept playing out of sight when you scrolled down or opened a title, so a title page's trailer had to share the computer with it. It now stops as soon as you can't see it and starts again when you come back.

items.title: Smoother in Firefox
items.text: The banner trailer asked YouTube for more than full HD, which many computers have to decode without help from the graphics card, so it stuttered in Firefox. Trailers now stay at 1080p, and the page's little glowing animations rest while one plays.

items.title: Trailers sit higher on phones
items.text: On phones a playing trailer started far down the title page, under a big empty gap. It now sits right below the close button.

title: Deleting a season stops its download

items.title: No more waiting for a download you deleted
items.text: Deleting a season or a show while it was still downloading only removed the finished episodes, and the rest kept downloading and came back. Delete now cancels the download and any conversion straight away, and the season's Delete button shows up even before the first episode is ready.

items.title: Trailer and title side by side
items.text: On a computer a playing trailer filled the whole window and pushed the title off the bottom. It now plays in a frame on top of the blurred picture, with the title still in view below.

items.title: Trailer on wide screens
items.text: On a computer the Trailer button on a title's page could sit under the title text, so clicking it did nothing. It's on top now and plays the trailer.

title: Finished downloads become playable right away

items.title: No more stuck "Almost ready"
items.text: A film's page left open while it downloaded could stay on "Almost ready 100%" after it finished, and you had to reload to play it. The page now switches to the film by itself.

title: Play now shows how long until it starts

items.title: Clearer Play now wait
items.text: While Play now gets the start of a video, the percentage and time now count toward starting playback, not the whole download. So you see "40% · about 30 s to go" instead of "0% downloaded · about 2 h left".

title: Big downloads don't stall at the start

items.title: No more "moving" pause
items.text: A big download could stop for a few minutes just after it started while the server shuffled it to a faster drive (Lost in Translation sat at 4 %). New downloads now start on that drive straight away, so they keep going.

title: Undo, thumbs down that counts, and more

items.title: Thumbs down hides it
items.text: Titles you give a thumbs down no longer show up in your Discover rows, Documentaries or Popular on Lilin. Search still finds them, and taking the thumbs down back brings them back.

items.title: Undo after deleting
items.text: After you delete something, you get a few seconds to press Undo before it's really gone.

items.title: Play now is on its way
items.text: While a download fetches the start of the video, it says so ("Play now in a moment"), so you know the Play now button is coming.

items.title: Tidy Continue watching
items.text: Each Continue watching card has a ⋯ button: Mark as watched, or Remove from Continue watching (your place is kept and it comes back when you watch it again).

items.title: Night mode remembers the show
items.text: Turn on night mode during a show and it's on again for that show's next episodes. Other shows and films start with it off.

items.title: Stray "false" text
items.text: Some sheets, like Browse while you're in Documentaries, showed the word "false" where nothing should be. Gone everywhere.

items.title: English documentaries only
items.text: With Lilin in English, Documentaries now only shows titles that were made in English: the SVT Play, Swedish and Nordic rows are gone, and the other rows leave out foreign-language films and shows. With Lilin in Swedish nothing changes.

items.title: Documentary genres on phones
items.text: The genre rows under Documentaries were wider than a phone screen, so the whole page shrank and the posters looked tiny. The rows now fit and swipe sideways, and the page is full size again.

items.title: Removed films
items.text: When a film you have open leaves your library, its page now shows a tidy card with a Back to your library button instead of a bare heading on a coloured background.

items.title: Featurettes stay out of your library
items.text: Downloads that came with bonus material (featurettes, interviews, trailers) listed each bonus video as another "version" of the film, and Delete all versions didn't go through. Bonus folders are now left out of the library, and deleting the film removes them with it.

title: Film pages stay put, X closes once

items.title: No false "Removed from your library"
